-- Spine excludes the 1900-01-01 parse-failure sentinel so the calendar covers
-- only real reporting history.
with bounds as (

    select
        min(date) as first_date,
        max(date) as last_date
    from "opcrime_dbt"."main"."stg_crimes"
    where date > '1901-01-01'

), spine as (

    select unnest(generate_series(first_date, last_date, interval 1 day)) as date_day
    from bounds

)

select
    cast(date_day as date)          as date_day,
    year(date_day)                  as year,
    month(date_day)                 as month,
    day(date_day)                   as day,
    quarter(date_day)               as quarter,
    week(date_day)                  as week,
    dayofweek(date_day)             as day_of_week,
    dayname(date_day)               as day_name,
    monthname(date_day)             as month_name,
    dayofweek(date_day) in (0, 6)   as is_weekend,
    strftime(date_day, '%Y-%m')     as year_month,
    strftime(date_day, '%Y-%m-%d')  as date_str

from spine

select *
from "opcrime_dbt"."main"."stg_crime_details"

-- One row per complaint number, classifying why it repeats. The two problem
-- classes have different owners: republication is an ingest bug, collision is a
-- source data issue we flag rather than repair.
with grouped as (

    select
        complaint_num,
        count(*)                       as row_count,
        count(distinct date)           as distinct_dates,
        count(distinct offense)        as distinct_offenses,
        count(distinct location)       as distinct_locations,
        count(distinct pdf_filename)   as distinct_pdfs
    from "opcrime_dbt"."main"."stg_crimes"
    where complaint_num is not null
    group by complaint_num

)

select
    *,
    case
        when row_count = 1 then 'unique'
        when distinct_dates > 1
          or distinct_offenses > 1
          or distinct_locations > 1 then 'collision'
        when distinct_pdfs > 1 then 'republished'
        else 'other_duplicate'
    end as quality_class

from grouped

-- Ports prepare_crime_db.py assign_zones(), including its nearest-zone snap.
-- The snap is a real business rule, not an implementation detail: edge-street
-- geocodes on Harlem, Austin and North Ave land just outside the village polygon
-- and would otherwise be dropped. Omitting it moves 1627 rows.
with pts as (

    select
        record_id,
        lat,
        long,
        case when lat is not null then ST_Point(long, lat) end as pt
    from "opcrime_dbt"."main"."stg_crimes"

), candidates as (

    select
        p.record_id,
        z.zone_id,
        z.zone_name,
        ST_Contains(z.zone_geom, p.pt) as contained,
        ST_Distance(p.pt, z.zone_geom) as dist
    from pts as p
    cross join "opcrime_dbt"."main"."stg_policing_zones" as z
    where p.pt is not null

), best as (

    select
        record_id,
        zone_id,
        zone_name,
        contained,
        dist,
        count(*) filter (where contained) over (partition by record_id) as contain_count
    from candidates
    qualify row_number() over (
        partition by record_id
        order by contained desc, dist asc, zone_id asc
    ) = 1

)

select
    p.record_id,
    p.lat,
    p.long,
    case when b.contained or b.dist < 0.0005 then b.zone_id   end as zone_id,
    case when b.contained or b.dist < 0.0005 then b.zone_name end as zone_name,
    coalesce(b.contain_count, 0) > 1 as zone_boundary_ambiguous,
    case
        when p.lat is null                                   then 'ungeocoded'
        when b.contained                                     then 'in_village'
        when b.dist < 0.0005   then 'snapped'
        else 'outside_village'
    end as zone_status

from pts as p
left join best as b using (record_id)

-- Same incident ingested twice because OPPD republished the report under a new
-- filename (-v2 against -v3, or an -02 suffix). Currently 45 groups, 48 rows
-- double counted downstream. Flagged not fixed: the repair belongs in
-- drop_exact_source_duplicates. See dbt_writeup.md.

select
    complaint_num,
    count(*)                                 as row_count,
    string_agg(distinct pdf_filename, ' | ') as filenames

from "opcrime_dbt"."main"."crimes"
where complaint_num is not null
group by complaint_num
having count(*) > 1
   and count(distinct date) = 1
   and count(distinct offense) = 1
   and count(distinct location) = 1
   and count(distinct pdf_filename) > 1

select offense_text
from "opcrime_dbt"."main"."dim_offense"
where offense_text is null

select
    offense_text as unique_field,
    count(*) as n_records

from "opcrime_dbt"."main"."dim_offense"
where offense_text is not null
group by offense_text
having count(*) > 1

-- Flags republication double counts without dropping them. Removing rows here
-- would change published counts silently; downstream picks the filter.
-- Highest filename sorts last for the -v2/-v3 and -02 suffix conventions.
with ranked as (

    select
        c.*,
        q.quality_class,
        case
            when q.quality_class = 'republished'
            then row_number() over (
                partition by c.complaint_num
                order by c.pdf_filename desc
            )
            else 1
        end as republication_rank
    from "opcrime_dbt"."main"."stg_crimes" as c
    left join "opcrime_dbt"."main"."int_complaint_quality" as q
        on c.complaint_num = q.complaint_num

)

select
    *,
    republication_rank > 1 as is_duplicate_republication
from ranked

select record_id
from "opcrime_dbt"."main"."int_crimes_deduplicated"
where record_id is null

having count(*) > 1

-- Geometry is dropped here; parquet has no native GEOMETRY type and no consumer
-- needs the polygon, only the label.

from "opcrime_dbt"."main"."stg_policing_zones" as z
left join "opcrime_dbt"."main"."int_crimes_zoned" as c

from "opcrime_dbt"."main"."stg_geocode_cache"

-- Distinguishes a cache miss from a cached known-unresolvable; collapsing the two
-- would make the 21 unresolvable locations look like work to redo every night.
select
    c.record_id,
    c.source,
    c.location,
    c.location_key_naive,
    c.lat  as pipeline_lat,
    c.long as pipeline_long,
    g.lat  as cache_lat,
    g.long as cache_long,
    case
        when g.location_key is null   then 'miss'
        when g.known_unresolvable     then 'known_unresolvable'
        else 'hit'
    end as cache_status,
    c.lat is not null as pipeline_has_coords

from "opcrime_dbt"."main"."stg_crimes" as c
left join "opcrime_dbt"."main"."stg_geocode_cache" as g
    on c.location_key_naive = g.location_key

with all_values as (

-- Makes the known defects queryable rather than buried in test logs. The docs
-- site renders test definitions but not outcomes, so this model is how a reader
-- sees what is actually wrong with the data.
with checks as (

    select 'republished_pdf_rows' as issue,
           'Same incident ingested twice under a revised PDF filename' as description,
           'ingest bug, fix in drop_exact_source_duplicates' as owner,
           count(*) as row_count
    from "opcrime_dbt"."main"."fct_incidents"
    where is_duplicate_republication

    union all
    select 'complaint_collisions',
           'One complaint number on materially different incidents',
           'source data, flag only',
           count(*)
    from "opcrime_dbt"."main"."fct_incidents"
    where complaint_quality_class = 'collision'

    union all
    select 'ungeocoded',
           'No coordinates resolved',
           'run a Python cache-fill',
           count(*)
    from "opcrime_dbt"."main"."fct_incidents"
    where lat is null

    union all
    select 'geocode_cache_miss',
           'Location absent from the shared geocode cache under the naive key',
           'needs location_key published upstream',
           count(*)
    from "opcrime_dbt"."main"."fct_incidents"
    where geocode_cache_status = 'miss'

    union all
    select 'outside_village',
           'Geocoded outside the 8 policing zone polygons',
           'expected, not a defect',
           count(*)
    from "opcrime_dbt"."main"."fct_incidents"
    where zone_status = 'outside_village'

    union all
    select 'date_sentinel',
           'Date failed to parse and fell back to 1900-01-01',
           'source data, flag only',
           count(*)
    from "opcrime_dbt"."main"."fct_incidents"
    where date <= '1901-01-01'

    union all
    select 'date_future',
           'Incident date is in the future',
           'source data, poisons naive freshness checks',
           count(*)
    from "opcrime_dbt"."main"."fct_incidents"
    where date > current_date

    union all
    select 'pdf_dashboard_date_mismatch',
           'PDF and dashboard disagree on the incident date by a day or more',
           'flagged in merge_notes, not repaired',
           count(*)
    from "opcrime_dbt"."main"."fct_incidents"
    where date_mismatch

)

select
    issue,
    description,
    owner,
    row_count,
    round(100.0 * row_count / (select count(*) from "opcrime_dbt"."main"."fct_incidents"), 2) as pct_of_rows
from checks
order by row_count desc

select
    offense,
    primary_crime_against,
    strftime(date, '%Y-%m')       as year_month,
    year(date)                    as year,
    count(*)                      as incident_count,
    count(distinct zone_id)       as zones_touched,
    count(*) filter (where zone_status = 'outside_village') as outside_village_count

from "opcrime_dbt"."main"."fct_incidents"
where date > '1901-01-01'
  and offense is not null
group by offense, primary_crime_against, year_month, year

select
    zone_id,
    zone_name,
    zone_status,
    strftime(date, '%Y-%m')                     as year_month,
    year(date)                                  as year,
    month(date)                                 as month,
    count(*)                                    as incident_count,
    count(*) filter (where not is_duplicate_republication) as deduplicated_count,
    count(distinct complaint_num)               as distinct_complaints,
    count(*) filter (where primary_crime_against = 'Person')   as crimes_against_person,
    count(*) filter (where primary_crime_against = 'Property') as crimes_against_property,
    count(*) filter (where primary_crime_against = 'Society')  as crimes_against_society

from "opcrime_dbt"."main"."fct_incidents"
where date > '1901-01-01'
group by zone_id, zone_name, zone_status, year_month, year, month
